career_ladder.note: Fire and Rescue Officers (Trainee) serve in the Kerala Fire and Rescue Services Department responding to urban and rural fires, floods, building collapses, and natural disasters. After completing 6 months mandatory basic training at the State Fire Academy (Viyyur, Thrissur), recruits advance through Leading Fireman, Station Officer, Assistant Divisional Officer, and Divisional Officer upon passing departmental technical examinations.

exam_scheme.note: Selection to Fire and Rescue Officer (Trainee) involves five progressive stages: Written OMR Examination (Objective type carrying 100 marks), Physical Measurement Test (PMT), Physical Efficiency Test (PET - National 1-star standard), Swimming Test (Compulsory 50-metre swimming test), and Medical Examination. Ranked lists are prepared on a statewide basis based strictly on marks obtained in the Written Examination among candidates who qualify all physical, swimming, and medical standards.

papers.paper_name: Physical Measurement (Male: Height min 165 cm [160 cm for SC/ST], Chest min 81 cm with 5 cm expansion [76 cm with 5 cm expansion for SC/ST], Weight min 50 kg)
papers.qualifying_threshold: Qualifying standard; candidate must fulfill prescribed minimum height, chest, and weight measurements

stages.source_label: Kerala PSC Fire Force PET Guidelines

papers.paper_name: PET Events (Must qualify in min 5 of 8 standard events: 100m in 14.0s, High Jump 132.2cm, Long Jump 457.2cm, Shot Put 609.6cm, Cricket Ball Throw 6096cm, Rope Climbing 365.8cm, Pull-ups 8 times, 1500m in 5m 44s)
papers.qualifying_threshold: Must qualify in at least 5 out of 8 prescribed athletic events

stages.source_label: Kerala Fire and Rescue Services Swimming Qualification Standards

papers.paper_name: Swimming Assessment (Candidate must swim a distance of 50 metres without any aid or lifebuoy within prescribed time)
papers.qualifying_threshold: Compulsory qualification; failure in swimming test leads to immediate disqualification

stages.source_label: Kerala Fire Force Medical Manual & Vision Standards

papers.paper_name: Medical Fitness & Vision Assessment (Distant vision 6/6 each eye, near vision 0.5 without glasses, normal colour vision, free from respiratory and cardiac infirmities)
papers.qualifying_threshold: Fitness certificate from authorized Government Medical Board

financial_package.note: Fire and Rescue Officers in Kerala Fire and Rescue Services are remunerated under the Kerala State 11th Pay Revision (G.O.(P) No. 27/2021/Fin) at Pay Scale ₹27,900 - ₹63,700 with entry basic pay of ₹27,900.
financial_package.pay_source_label: Kerala PSC Gazette Notification Cat. No. 714/2021 & Kerala Fire and Rescue Services Department Pay Rules
financial_package.estimate_note: Calculated on Kerala State 11th Pay Revision entry basic pay of ₹27,900 with standard 58% DA (effective 1 Jul 2025, ₹16,182) plus House Rent Allowance (Class A Corporation ₹2,790, Class B Municipalities ₹1,900, Class C Panchayats ₹1,300), Fire Hazard/Risk allowance (₹1,200/month), and Uniform maintenance grant; net in-hand reflects statutory deductions for National Pension System (NPS, 10% on Basic+DA = ₹4,408), MEDISEP health insurance (₹500/month), State Life Insurance (SLI), and Professional Tax.
official_perks: Departmental fire station barracks accommodation or quarters allotment in municipal/corporation areas
Annual uniform maintenance allowance and firefighting protective equipment kit provided by department
Comprehensive cashless hospitalization coverage under the Kerala Government MEDISEP scheme
Hazard / special disaster response compensatory allowance during flood rescue and major emergencies
Onam festival bonus / special advance and Kerala Fire Force Benevolent Fund support
